sources.citation: Njoya, Ibirahim. 2010 (March). Précis d'orthographe pour la langue pana. Yaoundé: Association Camerounaise pour la Traduction de la Bible et l'Alphabétisation (CABTAL). 21 pp. (18 numbered). SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 47883.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 3 'Les tons' (printed pp. 9-13, PDF pp. 12-16): four phonemic tones — two level (H, L) and two contour (LH rising, HL falling); LH occurs only on long vowels, so short-vowel monosyllables carry only H, L, HL; minimal pairs given; a grammatical raising of the first verb syllable in the exhortative future (L→H, H→super-high). Nothing at all on stress / accent d'intensité / prominence — the only 'accent' words are the diacritic names (accent aigu, grave, circonflexe).

sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives / SIL Cameroon catalogue for pnz (entries 47883, 52640, 9525) and archived SIL Cameroon Pana language page (2016).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Catalogue only: SIL holds exactly three items for Pana — Njoya 2010 and the two versions of Seguin's survey; no phonology, grammar or dictionary of Pana is listed.

sources.citation: Seguin, Lawrence M. 2012 [1991]. The Eastern Mbum Survey: An Assessment of the Extendability of Current Language Development Projects. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2012-039. Dallas: SIL International. 225 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic / lexicostatistic survey of Karang, Kuo, Nzakambay, Pana, Mbere etc. (Pana mentioned 112 times, all in survey/intelligibility context); no phonological description; the word 'accents' appears only in a Giles 1970 reference; 'tone' only in a remark that an orthography should write tone. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Pana language' (citing Ethnologue 18 and Binam Bikoi (ed.) 2012 Atlas linguistique du Cameroun (ALCAM), Yaoundé: CERDOTOLA; Blench 2004 Adamawa list).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Distribution and classification only; no phonological statement; ALCAM 2012 is an inventory/atlas, not opened.

sources.citation: Elders, Stefan. 2006. Issues in comparative Kebi-Benue (Adamawa). Africana Linguistica 12: 37-88. doi:10.3406/aflin.2006.962 (Persée, open access).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative paper; Pana figures only in the classification discussion (pp. 42-43: Pana/Pondo/Gonge/Man dialect confusion in Ethnologue; Samarin 1971; CAR atlas treats all CAR Adamawa varieties as dialects of Pana). Section 3.4 'Tone' (pp. 58-59) quotes Boyd 1989a:202-203: 'All the Southern languages of the Mbum group (Adamawa A.6.C) also have two [tone levels], but the remaining subgroups have three'. No Pana tone data of its own; nothing on stress anywhere in the paper.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0, inventory 1633 'Pana (GM)', contributed by Christopher Green & Steven Moran, source Njoya 2010.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Segment inventory derived from Njoya 2010 listing tonemes ˦ (H), ˨ (L), ˥˩ (HL), ˩˥ (LH); no stress information (PHOIBLE does not record stress).

sources.citation: Boyd, Raymond. 1974. Étude comparative dans le groupe Adamawa. Paris: SELAF (Bibliothèque de la SELAF 46). 101 pp.

sources.note: The only comparative wordlist source that Elders 2006 implies covers Pana (he notes Pondo/Gonge/Tali were NOT in Boyd 1974); Boyd's Mbum-group lists are tone-marked and his introductory notes may state the prosodic type; would be the primary behind Boyd 1989a's 'two tone levels' claim.
